analysis.title: The Commodities Feed: False US-Iran hopes or the real deal?
key_insights: ICE Brent settled 7.6% lower on 2 Nov and fell back below $105/bbl on new hopes for US-Iran talks. ING notes similar hopes have appeared before with nothing materialising.

Positive signals came from both sides. President Trump answered "no" when asked whether he would strike Iran after the midterm elections, and Iran's president said the government has more authority from the supreme leader to negotiate with the US.
ING says it is too early to conclude escalation risks have passed. On Monday the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island, reportedly in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft.
Strong signs of progress in peace talks would mean more downside for oil. ING says the market still carries a large risk premium, particularly given the strong oil flows from the Persian Gulf.

TTF European gas settled 8.7% lower on the day at a little under EUR95/MWh on the US-Iran hopes. ING says de-escalation matters more for gas because LNG flows from the region have recovered less than oil flows.
Gas market is vulnerable heading deeper into the European heating season because LNG flows from the Gulf have not recovered.

Gold settled 1.85% higher on Monday, rebounding from its lowest level in a year after last week's sharp sell-off. Lower oil eased inflation concerns that had weighed on gold, and bargain hunting added support.

Gold has been caught in a broader risk-off move and heavy selling across technology stocks. ING expects some recovery after the correction but sees the near-term outlook as challenging because of expectations for higher rates and a stronger dollar.

sector_views.rationale: Prices fell sharply on US-Iran talk hopes, but a large risk premium remains and ING says it is too early to treat escalation risk as over. Progress in talks would mean more downside.
Gold expected to regain some ground after the correction, but higher rate expectations and a stronger dollar limit a sustained recovery.
